milestones.name: Where we actually started
milestones.summary: 10 realised trades, all losers. Expectancy −367 CAD/trade, lifetime −15,935 CAD. The live map held one strategy that emitted zero signals when computed honestly. Honest valuation as a trading business: ~$0.
milestones.plain: The baseline, written down without flattery. Ten real trades, ten losses, and the one strategy that was live turned out to be running on a bug.

milestones.name: Honest zero
milestones.summary: Nothing in the live map that cannot fire in real time. `Range_Stochastic_Divergence` struck off via `INTEGRITY_DISQUALIFIED`; regimes re-fit with corrected label ordering and causal smoothing (kappa ≥ 0.83); finding B re-tested against honest labels and it stands.
milestones.plain: The measured value stayed at zero — but it became a true zero. Every measurement taken after this point can be trusted, which is the only reason the rungs above it mean anything.
milestones.falsifier: If the map still routes to a strategy whose honest signal count is zero, M1 is not met regardless of what else was built.

milestones.name: First honest qualifier
milestones.summary: Three cells now sit in the live map as `qualified` — but only after the OOS gate was lowered from 60 months to 12 on 2026-08-21, and they rest on 5, 13 and 20 out-of-sample trades. Their profit factors (6.8–13.6) and drawdowns (0.02%–1%) are small-sample artefacts, stated as such by the owner. Measured against the original gates, the strongest honest candidate remains `demark_fractal_breakout` USD_JPY H4: 610 OOS trades, PF 1.51, Sharpe 1.11 — one passing cell in roughly 230.
milestones.plain: On paper, three strategies passed. In practice they passed because the bar was lowered and because nothing checks how many trades the evidence contains — five trades is not a track record. The one result that would genuinely count has 610 trades behind it and works on a single currency pair.
milestones.falsifier: A qualifier that would not survive re-imposing the 60-month gate and a minimum trade count is not a qualifier; it is a sample-size artefact.

milestones.name: Forward test
milestones.summary: A signal travels the full three-system path on the practice account and its realised results track expectation. The drill design is specified: System 1 publishes one correctly-formed signal carrying `"drill": true`, System 3 processes it through the full risk path with the flag intact, System 2 runs it to the broker call and stops, logging the order it would have sent. Evidence since recorded: on 2026-08-24 a signal traversed System 1 -> Pub/Sub -> relay -> System 3 -> System 2 -> OANDA and produced three real fills (2617 / 2621 / 2625), with `correlation_id = signal_id` intact at each hop. The transport half of this rung is therefore demonstrated; what remains is a clean drill with the flag preserved, and realised results that track expectation.
milestones.plain: Prove the pipe before trusting it with anything. One clearly-marked test order is sent down the whole chain; the last machine stops just short of actually placing it and writes down exactly what it would have done.
milestones.falsifier: If the same `signal_id` is not visible at all three systems, the pipe is not proven, however healthy each machine looks on its own.

milestones.name: Verified track record
milestones.summary: A continuous, auditable, out-of-sample equity curve of sufficient length to underwrite. This is the asset. Everything before it is infrastructure.
milestones.plain: A long enough run of honest results that somebody else would take it seriously. Buyers underwrite an equity curve first and inspect the engineering second.
milestones.falsifier: A curve with a gap, a restatement, or an unexplained parameter change in the middle is not a track record.

goals.title: Prove the signal pipe end to end across all three computers

metric.name: Signals decided at all three systems
metric.note: S2/S3 reply 2026-09-03: 9 published, 9 acked, 9 decided, 3 became real OANDA orders

goals.why: Signals route `S1 → Scored_Signal_Queue → S3 → AMS_Outbound_Queue → S2`. System 1 publishes to link 1 and that is verified. Links 2 and 3 are unverified and System 1 is blind to them — its service account is publisher-only and cannot list topics or subscriptions. Nothing else about model quality can matter until a message is observed arriving.
goals.plain: Three machines, two pipes between them. We can prove letters are going into the first pipe. Nobody has yet confirmed in writing that anyone is collecting them, or where the reply goes.
goals.definition_of_done: A written reply from System 3 naming its subscription on `Scored_Signal_Queue`, confirming a consumer is actually pulling it, and naming the topic it publishes approved orders to. Not 'it should be set up'. Then the same `signal_id` observed at all three systems during the drill.

Per System 2's own trace (2026-08-27): the execution engine stopped 2026-08-24T17:07:55Z alongside System 3's gate, no restart since, no exception logged. Its only runtime window this week (10:52-17:07 Monday) shows no order or fill events at all — zero OANDA fills, confirmed operational rather than risk-gate related. goals.title: Raise the producer cadence to at least hourly

metric.name: Producer runs per trading day
metric.note: Confirmed via `crontab -l` and a full week of `logs/cron_hourly_signals.log` (2026-08-24 through 2026-08-27): hourly cron at :15, 24 runs/day.

goals.why: The producer fires from `cron_daily_ingest_and_signals.sh` at 22:30 on weekdays. Two of the three live strategies are H4 — six bars a day — so a once-daily batch emits signals for bars that closed up to twenty hours earlier. `src/signals/run.py` already supports a continuous 60-second loop.
goals.plain: Trade ideas are posted once a night, but most of the strategies produce a new idea every four hours. Almost everything posted is describing a moment that has already gone.
goals.definition_of_done: `crontab -l` shows the producer running at least hourly during market hours. Recommendation on record: hourly cron before continuous service — smaller change, restartable, matches the existing operational pattern.

dependencies.need: Done 2026-08-2x: hourly cron installed (`shell/cron_hourly_signals.sh`, :15 past every hour). Verified against a full week of logs — 46 real signals published Mon-Wed, 0 dead-lettered.

Cadence is not cosmetic for us: the `ScoredSignal` TTL is 15 minutes. A once-daily 22:30 batch produces signals that are hours past that TTL on arrival, so they are discarded before any risk logic runs. Hourly is the minimum at which H4 signals survive the trip.

goals.title: Resolve ADR-001 — decide where live inference runs

metric.name: Approvals received
metric.note: Both approvals in as of 2026-08-22, each with conditions. System 3's envelope change must land BEFORE System 2 starts publishing, not after.

goals.why: Two incompatible architectures are on record. The code makes trading depend on Computer 1 — a host with unreliable networking — so if that machine is offline, nothing trades anywhere. That coupling is in no design document and is the direct cause of the incident in which the producer had never emitted a message and nobody could see why.
goals.plain: The whole operation currently depends on the least reliable computer in the building being awake. The proposal is to move the live work onto the machine that is already awake during market hours, and let the research machine go back to sleep.
goals.definition_of_done: System 2 and System 3 each reply APPROVE or REJECT with reasons, against their actual implementations rather than against the document. No implementation starts before both approve.

dependencies.need: Authored the ADR; would decommission its producer in the same change that enables System 2 inference

Reviewed 2026-08-22 — **approve with conditions**. Would run inference; already runs verified artifact sync and live HMM inference. Conditions: prove the transport first, sign the manifest rather than only checksumming it, run bundle strategy code in a least-privilege process with no broker credential, and gate cutover on a determinism test against System 1's own outputs.

Reviewed 2026-08-22 — **approve with conditions**. Responsibilities are unchanged and the publisher's identity is irrelevant to the gate. The envelope is not: it needs a required `producer`, a `bundle_id`, and a `drill` boolean, and that change must land before System 2 starts publishing, not after.

goals.title: Add a minimum trade-count gate to vetting

metric.name: Live cells below a defensible sample size

goals.why: `vet.py` treats `trade_count` only as a ranking tie-break, so there has never been a rule about how much evidence a qualification rests on. Combined with the 2026-08-21 reduction of `oos_months` from 60 to 12, cells with 5, 13 and 20 trades reached the live map with profit factors of 6.8 to 13.6.
goals.plain: Nothing in the examiner checks how many trades a strategy's track record actually contains. A strategy with five trades can therefore score spectacularly and be waved through — but five trades is noise.
goals.definition_of_done: A minimum trade-count gate exists in `gates.py` with a stated threshold and a test, and no cell below it can appear in a published map. Worth adding regardless of where the `oos_months` value finally lands.

dependencies.need: Implement the gate and re-run vetting

Sizing is derived from the measured edge, so a thin cell produces an unreliable Kelly fraction. In practice the sizing layer already refuses on insufficient or stale live statistics — 1,100 of 4,091 rejections to date — so the protection exists, but it arrives as a refusal to size rather than as a refusal to qualify.

goals.title: Fix qualified strategies published with empty exits
goals.why: All three entries in the current live map carry `exits: {}`. A strategy with no exit specification serializes cleanly and passes every schema check, but means nothing to whoever has to execute it — the executing system has been told when to enter and never told when to leave.
goals.plain: Every strategy currently live says how to open a trade and says nothing at all about how to close one. It looks perfectly valid to every automated check on the way out.
goals.definition_of_done: `vet.py` refuses to publish a cell with an empty `exits` object, with a guarding test. The three live entries either gain exits or leave the map.

dependencies.need: Fix the defect in `vet.py`
Position management executes exit parameters carried on the order; with none supplied there is nothing to execute, and trailing stops and time-based exits are inert.

Layer `H` compares the maximum hold duration against the next Friday cutoff. With `exits: {}` it falls back to the configured maximum rather than the strategy's own — 131 rejections have already landed there.

goals.title: Make System 1 survivable — backups, CI and its own alerting
goals.why: Audited 2026-08-28: there is no database backup script anywhere in the repository, no CI configuration (`.github/workflows/` does not exist), and no alarm on System 1's own side when it stops emitting. The database holds 4.7M price rows and 93k trade outcomes representing months of compute — a disk failure loses all of it with no recovery path. The 2026-08-24 outage, undetected for three days, is the same lesson from the other end of the pipe.

goals.title: Put the gatekeeper back into the live decision path

metric.name: Live signals carrying a model score
metric.note: 9 of 9 scored, 0 unscored (signal_emitter_state.json 2026-09-03). The scoring half is DONE; the gate half is not — see definition_of_done

goals.why: **The original premise of this goal was wrong and is retracted.** It said every live signal is emitted UNSCORED with `MISSING_FEATURE`. Measured 2026-08-30: scoring works — 15/15 (pair x granularity), all live-map strategies known to the model, `signals_unscored_total: 0`. That claim came from a stale code comment and was corrected in `TO-SYSTEM2-3-2026-08-30-erratum-the-gatekeeper-does-score-live.md`. What is actually broken is narrower and worse: the gatekeeper applies **no threshold at inference**. `Scorer.score()` never loads the manifest and `run.py` stamps a hardcoded 0.5 onto the wire as `threshold_applied`, below every calibrated cutoff (0.60-0.80). No below-threshold refusal exists, so the live approval rate is undefined, not zero. Separately (O-17) the scorer loads `models/` directly rather than a pointer, so it is running `champion_model.pkl` `23b6d4ca` — an artifact that was never published, while the wire claims `gk-d614163c`.
goals.plain: The quality filter does look at every trade and does produce a score. What it never does is act on it — the cutoff it compares against is a placeholder low enough that nothing is ever refused. And the model doing the scoring is not the one the message says it is.
goals.definition_of_done: Two things, and the second is a decision not a code change. (1) O-17 closed: the scorer loads the published pointer, so `gatekeeper_model_sha256` on the wire matches the artifact that actually scored. (2) The shadow review is written up after 7 days of live data (from the 2026-08-30 open) and an activate / stay-shadow decision is recorded. Switching the gate on today refuses ~14 of 15 live map cells; that is the calibration working (`shipped_approval_rate` 0.079), so it is a trading-activity decision. Owner decided 2026-08-30: shadow. **Do not activate it as a bug fix.**

goals.title: Repair telemetry — no dead panels, no numbers without a source

metric.name: Dashboard panels serving live data
metric.note: Six DB-backed panels still render "awaiting endpoint"

goals.why: Telemetry is the only surface anyone actually looks at, and today it is partly blind. `CONNECTIONS.md` lists six panels — breakers, state transitions, sizing, fills, notifications, override audit — as `v2` awaiting a read endpoint, while the data already sits in the database. System 2's `/status` advertises a `gatekeeper` block that reads `{"state": "unavailable", "reason": "no approval-rate provider wired"}`, so the tile is empty *and* the watchdog check that depends on it can never fire. And `db_client.py` still carries an `ALLOW_SQLITE_FALLBACK` path that caches a degraded SQLite engine forever — a telemetry backend that keeps answering after it has lost the real database is worse than one that stops.
goals.plain: The dashboard has holes in it. Some boxes are blank because nobody built the small piece of plumbing behind them, and one part can quietly switch to a spare copy of the database and keep showing numbers as if nothing happened. Before telemetry can be trusted as the place you look, the blanks have to fill in and every number has to say where it came from.
goals.definition_of_done: Every panel on the dashboard either renders live data or states exactly which endpoint it is waiting on and why; no panel shows a constant; the gatekeeper provider is wired; and the SQLite fallback cannot be reached by anything a person reads.

dependencies.need: Its health and model-set fields are surfaced but need no change
Owns the publisher, the backend and the dashboard
Must serve the six DB-backed read endpoints from the Guardian

goals.title: Make telemetry the single source of truth, fed by a live stream
goals.why: Right now telemetry is a derived view assembled by polling: the dashboard polls four HTTP surfaces every three seconds and the publisher writes GCS snapshots, so what you see is a reconstruction, not the event. Broker state only reaches telemetry through System 2's `/status`, which is why OANDA reporting `pendingOrderCount: 6` while `ams_open_positions` holds `sl = None, tp = None` for all three open trades was invisible until someone read both by hand. Every decision, fill and account change should land in one store as it happens, stamped with its source, so that divergence between broker-truth and system-truth is a visible alert rather than an archaeology exercise.
goals.plain: At the moment the dashboard keeps asking "anything new?" and stitches an answer together. It should instead be told the moment something happens, by each system directly — the broker included — and every number should carry a label saying who said it and when. Then when two sources disagree, the screen shows the disagreement instead of hiding it.
goals.definition_of_done: OANDA, System 1, System 2 and System 3 all push into one telemetry store; the dashboard receives updates over a stream rather than a 3-second poll; every field carries `source` and `as_of`; and a broker-vs-system divergence raises an alert without a human comparing two screens.

Owns the publisher, the streaming backend and the broker feed
Publish every gate decision and fill as it happens, not only into `ams.db`

goals.title: Give telemetry a safe operator control plane
goals.why: Screen 4 of the dashboard already carries the full two-step confirm interface, but nothing is wired: confirming an action tells the operator which CLI command to go and type. Every real control path — `/pause`, `/unquarantine`, `/mode enforce` — runs through the Telegram bot and `ams.ctl` on `trading-1`, which means stopping the system requires SSH and knowing the vocabulary. That is the wrong latency for a force-stop. The counter-constraint is absolute and stays: the dashboard must never be the thing that flips the system to live.
goals.plain: The screen has the buttons drawn but they do not do anything — they just tell you what to go and type on the server. Stopping trading should not need a login and a memorised command. What the screen must never be able to do is turn live trading *on*; that stays double-locked.
goals.definition_of_done: An authenticated `POST /control` supports force-stop, per-pair or per-strategy opt-out, refresh, and a read-only debug view; every call is written to `override_audit` with the operator identity; the `go_live_enabled` gate remains unreachable from the dashboard; and a force-stop from the browser is demonstrated end to end on the practice account.

goals.title: Restore signal and trade alerting to Telegram

metric.name: Routed notification events with a live emitter
metric.note: 12 routed events have no emitter anywhere in `src/ams/`

goals.why: The Telegram channel is not broken — `service_started`, breaker alerts and override replies all deliver. What is missing is the emitters. `config/risk_config.json` routes `trade_opened`, `trade_closed_win`, `trade_closed_loss`, `signal_rejected`, `caution_entered`, `caution_exited`, `soft_stop`, `state_transition`, `stale_snapshot`, `publish_failure`, `daily_summary` and `weekly_report`, and not one of them has a matching `notifier(...)` call anywhere in `src/ams/`. The routing table describes a system that was never wired, so the operator gets paged about service restarts and never about trades.

goals.definition_of_done: Every event named in the notification routing table has an emitter and a rendered message; a live trade produces a Telegram message within one minute of the fill; and an alert fires if `notify_outbox` gains no row across an active trading session.

goals.title: Adopt a data governance and data-quality standard across build and deploy
goals.why: The failures found this month are governance failures wearing engineering clothes. `strategy_status` holds zero rows, so no per-strategy state is recorded anywhere. `risk_state.size_multiplier = 0` sits in the risk table with a `halted_until` that expired on 2026-07-28, evidently unread, because live decisions still produce non-zero units. 532 dead account snapshots sit in `ams-inbound.ams` and 532 more in its DLQ, oldest from July. System 1 shipped a model set with `code_dirty: true` and a `freshness_checks.overall_status: WARN` naming an outcomes feed 171 hours past its grace window. None of that is a bug in a function; all of it is the absence of an owner, a retention rule and a gate.
goals.plain: Several of the problems we keep finding are not broken code — they are data nobody owns. A table nobody fills in, a safety number nobody reads, a queue nobody drains, a model built from an unclean copy of the code. The fix is boring and permanent: every piece of data gets a named owner, a defined shape, a rule for how long it lives, and an automatic check that fails the build when it goes bad.
goals.definition_of_done: A written standard names, for every table, topic and published artifact: its owner, its schema of record, its retention rule and its lineage. Freshness, row-count, null-rate and referential checks run in the deploy path and fail a promotion. No artifact is publishable from a dirty working tree.

dependencies.need: Model set, feature store and outcomes feed must pass the same gates
Telemetry and regime tables come under the same ownership rules
Holds the contracts, migrations, audit ledger and export path the standard is enforced from

goals.title: Publish one operations handbook a human can change the system from
goals.why: Operational knowledge is scattered across `audit/communication/S2-*.md`, `CONNECTIONS.md`, `deployment-guide/`, `GO_LIVE.md`, `BACKUP.md` and the systemd units on `trading-1` — and it contradicts itself. `S2-REPLY-2026-08-27-signal-path-trace.md` states the processes died and never restarted, no relay unit exists, and this week's 46 signals never arrived; the live trace one day later shows all five units running, the relay enabled with a lifetime counter, 46 signals relayed and three real OANDA fills. Both documents are on file. A person deciding what to fix has no way to know which one is true, and no single place that tells them which credential or role they need to act.
goals.plain: The instructions for running this system live in a dozen documents, and two of them say opposite things about the same week. Anyone trying to debug it has to guess which is current. There should be one document, kept current, that a human can read and edit — how each service runs, how to read each screen, what to do when each known thing breaks, and exactly what access you need to do it.

goals.title: Turn every recurring job into a versioned skill or agent
goals.why: The same jobs are re-derived from scratch every time: the pipeline trace, the weekly readiness reply, queue and DLQ inspection, deploy verification, the telemetry panel audit, the cleanup pass. Quality varies by run, and the 08-27 trace is the proof — it reached five wrong conclusions because it read the local mirror instead of `trading-1`, a mistake a fixed procedure would have made impossible. There is no `.claude/skills` directory in the repository at all; every run starts from a blank prompt.
goals.plain: We keep asking for the same pieces of work, and each time the answer is built from nothing, so the quality moves around. One of those runs got five facts wrong because it read the wrong copy of the system. Writing the recurring jobs down as fixed, reusable procedures — with a stated output shape — makes the good version the default instead of the lucky one.
goals.definition_of_done: Each recurring job exists as a checked-in skill with a stated input, a fixed output contract and a verification step; two consecutive runs of the same skill on unchanged inputs produce materially the same report; and every skill that reads system state names `trading-1` as the source and the local checkout as a mirror.

goals.why: The pipe is not the problem any more. Signals on 08-25 and 08-26 were decided, sized and written to the outbound queue, and then none of them reached OANDA — for three distinct reasons. Four of the last six were stopped by `backup_guard` because a position from 2026-08-24 is still open on that pair, and since EUR_USD, GBP_USD and USD_CAD carry essentially all the flow, the strategy cannot re-enter on its own main pairs for as long as those three sit there. goals.plain: Orders are being made correctly and then blocked at the very last step. Three old trades from 24 August are still open and, by design, they lock out every new trade on the same currency pairs — which happen to be nearly all of them. Separately, the risk system approves sizes the trading system is not allowed to send, and something is producing trades with the stop-loss on the wrong side.
goals.definition_of_done: A decided signal on a main pair reaches OANDA and fills; the notional cap is a shared, versioned limit rather than a private constant; bracket direction is asserted at every hop that can construct one; and the three 08-24 positions have an explicit, recorded disposition.

goals.title: Harden the queue and Pub/Sub transport before the cloud cutover
goals.why: Two permanently-invalid messages — `drill-003`, missing `schema_version`, and a diagnostic `DIRECT-b61a5fab` — fail validation, are never acked, and redeliver roughly every six seconds forever. The relay's lifetime counter reads `forwarded: 48, rejected: 23,566`. The cause is structural: not one of the five subscriptions has a `deadLetterPolicy`, all sit at `ackDeadlineSeconds: 10`, and the `scored_signal_dlq` topic exists wired to nothing, so an invalid message has nowhere to go but round again. Alongside it, `scored-signals.heartbeat` has accumulated 9,511 rows in `ready` that no consumer subscribes to. Moving this transport into the cloud without fixing it moves a log-flooding retry loop into a billed environment.
goals.plain: Two bad messages from a test are stuck going round and round the system every six seconds, and have been for weeks — twenty-three thousand rejections against forty-eight real deliveries. Nothing was ever set up to catch a message that can never be processed, so it retries forever. There is also a queue quietly growing with nine and a half thousand messages nobody reads. All of this should be fixed before it is moved to the cloud, where it costs money to run in circles.
goals.definition_of_done: Every subscription has a dead-letter policy pointing at a real DLQ topic; the two poison messages are drained; the relay's rejected counter stops climbing while idle; no local queue grows without a consumer; and the stale `ams-inbound.ams` and `bridge.unrouted` backlogs are drained or explicitly routed.

tasks.title: Add producer, bundle id and drill to the contracts
tasks.detail: Deployed 2026-08-29, with one deliberate deviation to record. **All three fields shipped optional, including `producer`.** The plan called for `producer` to be `required` so an unexpected publisher is rejected outright during the transition — but the safe orders are opposite for the two changes: widening an `additionalProperties: false` consumer is consumer-accepts-first, while promoting a field to `required` is producer-emits-first, and System 1 had not yet enabled stamping. Agreed sequence: all three stay optional until one real drill completes after Sunday's open, then System 1 tells us before flipping them to `required` and we confirm we are reading them first. While `drill` is optional, absent is read as `false` (a real order) — the fail-safe reading, and unambiguous only because System 1 stamps the flag on every message including real ones. The contract change never shipped alone: it went out together with System 2's drill short-circuit, because the schema half on its own moves the system from *safely rejects* to *silently executes*. **Still open:** publication of the updated contracts to `gs://scalable-brain-artifacts/contracts/v1/` is not verified, and the `required` promotion of `producer` remains outstanding.

tasks.detail: System 2's remaining condition: cutover gated on a determinism test against System 1's own outputs. Ship a frozen input set with expected signal ids and scores so they can prove byte-equivalence rather than trusting it.

tasks.detail: The pipeline assumes a local PostgreSQL 16 + TimescaleDB. Either migrate to managed Postgres or keep model building local and ship only the bundle to the cloud. The rest of the migration hangs off this — decide it explicitly rather than by drift.

tasks.detail: The direct next step on T-112: audit logs are not enabled for Pub/Sub in this project, so the caller that drained the backlog cannot be recovered retroactively. Enable them, re-run the producer, and watch who acks in real time.

tasks.detail: Done 2026-09-03 by owner decision — the fuller record is T-143. The retrain cron is reinstalled at `0 * * * *` and `cron_holds.json` is empty, so the heartbeat now reports CRITICAL honestly instead of suppressing three checks. Two things were corrected in the same pass: the hold had been written by an agent session on 2026-08-15 and backdated with `declared_by: emmanuel`, and its 2026-09-15 expiry was invented — Computer 2 named no date. **This was 're-enable', not 'renew deliberately'.** First scheduled-window run is Sunday 2026-09-06 00:00 UTC.

tasks.title: Model spread, slippage and commission in the backtest
tasks.detail: OOS metrics are computed on mid prices. The three qualified cells rest on 5, 13 and 20 trades with drawdowns of 0.02%-1% — costs are plausibly larger than the entire measured edge, which would make them not merely thin but negative.

tasks.detail: `src/nlp/finbert.py` and `macro_scraper.py` already exist and feed nothing. Either connect them under the standard DQ and point-in-time gates, or retire them so the tree stops implying a capability that is not there.

tasks.detail: Carry and session overlap are cheap, well understood, and orthogonal to anything currently in the feature store.

tasks.detail: Five pairs across 47 strategies is a narrow base for any cross-sectional claim, and `src/portfolio/` is built to align many pairs onto one calendar already.

tasks.detail: Pub/Sub, storage, scheduler and any managed database have a running cost nobody has written down. A trading system with no edge yet should know its burn before it grows.

tasks.title: Decide the fate of the two 08-24 positions that are locking out the main pairs
tasks.detail:
**Corrected against the broker 2026-08-29T20:19Z.** Two positions remain open, not three — USD_CAD has since closed. Both were opened `2026-08-24T11:15` and have run 464,600 s (5.4 days):

| | EUR_USD | GBP_USD |
|---|---|---|
| trade | 2618 long 19,967u | 2622 long 18,602u |
| entry | 1.16647 | 1.36275 |
| stop | 1.15617 (103.0 pips) | 1.35147 (112.8 pips) |
| target | 1.18655 (200.8 pips) | 1.38409 (213.4 pips) |
| risk to stop | 205.66 USD | 209.83 USD |
| unrealized | −234.42 CAD | −251.05 CAD |

**They are stopped and bracketed — the earlier `sl = None, tp = None` was a mirror defect, not a naked position.** `ams_open_positions` still records no stop for either, and its `broker_trade_id` holds a UUID (`2863fca9-…`, `d1dbfe2c-…`) rather than the OANDA trade id, so the mirror cannot even be joined to the broker by key. The `recon:underinformed:EUR_USD` and `recon:underinformed:GBP_USD` watchdog episodes opened at 2026-08-29T19:33:33Z are that divergence being correctly reported — *broker has the stop, the mirror did not record it*. Left as-is rather than written into the live table: this is report-only, and the mirror is the thing to repair, not the row.

**The stops are the compressed ones.** 103.0 and 112.8 pips are exactly the placed distances from the 08-28 finding — System 1 sized these against 151.9 and 163.1 pips, so both positions carry a stop about a third tighter than the distance their size was computed from, and a correspondingly higher stop-out rate than the model assumes. The re-anchoring fix shipped 2026-08-28 and applies to new orders only; these two predate it and will not be repaired by it.

**Still the blocking question, and it is a trading decision.** `backup_guard` refuses any new order on a pair that already holds a position — it rejected four of the last six orders (signals `d48d503b`, `f5a19573`, `c2b3f00e`, `e8998559` across 08-26). EUR_USD and GBP_USD carry essentially all the signal flow, so the strategy cannot re-enter anywhere while these two sit there, and that resumes the moment the market reopens. Needs a recorded answer and a rule: how long may one position hold a pair hostage before it is force-reviewed?

tasks.title: Publish the §7.2 notional cap where System 3 can size against it
tasks.detail: AMS sized signal `a7d1ffbd` at 57,935 units of USD_JPY — 9,234,723 notional — and System 2 rejected it at the last line against a 5,000,000 cap that System 3 has no knowledge of. The cap must become a shared, versioned limit on the contract or on `/status`, not a constant private to the executor, or System 3 will keep approving orders that are structurally un-executable. Pairs with T-317.

tasks.title: Assert bracket direction at every hop that can construct one
tasks.detail: Signal `38503355` reached the broker call as `GBP_USD: BUY SL=1.361345 TP=1.374215 entry=1.36051` — the stop-loss above entry on a long. Same defect class as the `drill-003` test message, so it is not drill-only: something upstream inverts brackets on live signals. Catching it at the broker call is the last possible moment; the assertion belongs at the producer, in the contract schema, and in a test that fails on an inverted bracket.

tasks.title: Wire the gatekeeper approval-rate provider that `/status` already advertises
tasks.detail: System 2 `/status` returns `"gatekeeper": {"state": "unavailable", "reason": "no approval-rate provider wired"}`. Two things fail from that one gap: the dashboard's gatekeeper tile has nothing to render, and the watchdog's `s2:approval_rate` check can never fire, so a gatekeeper that silently starts rejecting everything would page nobody.

tasks.title: Serve the account tiles with a reconciliation stamp, not a bare number
tasks.detail: NAV, balance and margin reach the dashboard from `/status.account_summary` and nothing asserts they still match OANDA. Publish `reconciled_at` and the broker-vs-system delta alongside the value, and mark the tile stale when the delta or the age crosses a threshold. The dashboard already degrades honestly on unreachable services; it should degrade the same way on a number that is merely old.

tasks.title: Make the SQLite fallback unreachable in anything a person reads
tasks.detail: `db_client.py` falls back to `sqlite:///telemetry_fallback.db` when Postgres is unavailable and caches that engine in `_ENGINE_CACHE` — the code's own comment notes it would otherwise reuse the fallback forever. A telemetry backend that keeps answering after losing the real database produces confident wrong numbers, which is worse than an outage. Restrict it to tests, or make every response it serves carry a `degraded` flag the UI must render.

tasks.title: Retract the 08-27 signal-path trace and record the correction
tasks.detail: `S2-REPLY-2026-08-27-signal-path-trace.md` is on file as the current understanding and is wrong on five load-bearing points: it states both processes died Monday and never restarted, that no systemd unit exists for `pubsub_signal_relay.py`, that there are zero log lines for it, that this week's 46 signals never arrived, and that `0 APPROVED` means nothing completes the journey. The live trace a day later contradicts every one. Anything planned off that document is planned off fiction — mark it retracted at the top rather than deleting it, and link the correction.

tasks.title: Stand up the operations handbook as one living, human-editable document
tasks.detail: Today the operating knowledge is spread over `audit/communication/S2-*.md`, `telemetry-dashboard/CONNECTIONS.md`, `deployment-guide/`, `GO_LIVE.md`, `BACKUP.md`, `RESTORE.md` and the systemd units themselves. The handbook needs: every service and its unit on `trading-1`, how to read each health surface, what each decision label actually means, a playbook per known failure mode, and how to make a change safely. It must be editable by a human directly — not generated, not agent-only — and reviewed on a fixed cadence so it cannot rot into a second contradictory trace.

tasks.title: Write down the security envelope for every operator action
tasks.detail: A person cannot safely change a system whose access model is undocumented. For each action the handbook describes, state the secret, service account, IAM role and host required: the OANDA practice token, the Telegram bot token, the Pub/Sub publisher account, the GCS artifact bucket, Postgres on `34.52.232.110`, and the dashboard access token. Note as part of this that `link_to_telemetry.md` carries a live dashboard token and is only kept out of git by a `.gitignore` line — the envelope should say where such material is *supposed* to live.

tasks.title: Inventory the recurring jobs that should become skills
tasks.detail: Candidates already visible in the record: the live pipeline trace, the weekly readiness reply, queue and DLQ inspection, deploy verification, the telemetry panel audit, and the repository cleanup pass. For each, capture what it reads, what it must never read (the local mirror, when the question is about production), and the shape of the report it produces. This is the design step for G-020 — no skills are written yet.

tasks.title: Bring telemetry's tables under the governance standard
tasks.detail: Name the owner, schema of record, retention rule and lineage for `fact_live_trades`, `dim_asset`, `dim_strategy`, the regime grid, the GCS telemetry snapshots and the analytics mirror. State which of them is authoritative when two disagree — today `fact_live_trades`, the GCS snapshot and the broker can each be read as the answer to "what did we trade", and the September streaming work in G-015 will make that ambiguity worse before it makes it better.

tasks.title: Drain `bridge.unrouted` and stop the heartbeat topic growing
tasks.detail: `bridge.unrouted` holds 19 messages, all `control:STOPPED:signal:SIGTERM` shutdown events the bridge cannot route, newest at the 08-27 restart — confirming F-406. Separately `scored-signals.heartbeat` has 9,511 rows sitting in `ready` because nothing subscribes to that topic; it grows without bound. Either give each a consumer or stop publishing to it, and add a bound so an unconsumed local topic raises rather than accumulates.

tasks.title: Finish the streaming path and retire the 3-second poll
tasks.detail: Both halves already exist in skeleton — `cloud/telemetry-web/routes/streaming.py` on the backend and `src/hooks/useSSE.ts` in the dashboard — while `CONNECTIONS.md` still describes the transport as polling four HTTP surfaces every three seconds. Complete it so the dashboard is event-driven, with the poll retained only as a reconnect fallback, and bound the end-to-end latency from event to pixel.

tasks.title: Make OANDA a first-class telemetry source rather than a derived one
tasks.detail: Broker state reaches telemetry only through System 2's `/status`, so the system can only ever show its own opinion of the account. Publish OANDA's account and transaction stream into the telemetry store directly, beside the system's view, and alert on divergence — the `pendingOrderCount: 6` at the broker against `sl = None, tp = None` in `ams_open_positions` is exactly the class of gap this makes visible.

tasks.title: Stamp every telemetry field with its provenance
tasks.detail: Each value carries `source` (broker, system-1, system-2, system-3, derived) and `as_of`, and the UI renders both. A number with no provenance is indistinguishable from a hardcoded one, which is how the current class of "is this real?" question keeps arising.

tasks.title: Containerise System 2 and move its config off local disk
tasks.detail: There is no Dockerfile for the execution engine and its configuration lives in `config/.env.system2` on `trading-1`. The cutover in G-009 cannot proceed while the executor is a host-bound process with host-bound secrets. Pairs with System 1's T-126 and T-127.

tasks.title: Execute the three-process Pub/Sub cutover planned in T-211
tasks.detail: T-211 produces the plan; this is the change itself, run as one atomic switch across the relay, the bridge and the executor, with the local SQLite queue kept as a rollback path for one trading week before it is retired.

tasks.title: Freeze the v1 contract surface and version every change after it
tasks.detail: `ScoredSignal`, `ApprovedOrder`, `AccountSnapshot`, `FillEvent`, `Command` and `ProducerHeartbeat` are the interface between three independently-deployed systems, and both `ScoredSignal` and `ApprovedOrder` are `additionalProperties: false` — which is why T-308 blocks the drill. Land the outstanding field additions, then freeze: after the freeze, every change ships as a new version with both accepted during a stated overlap.

tasks.title: Build the first three skills and hold them to a rubric
tasks.detail: Start with the three highest-frequency jobs from T-221 — the pipeline trace, the queue and DLQ inspection, and deploy verification. Each states its inputs, its output contract, and a verification step; each names `trading-1` as the source of truth for live questions. Test: two runs on unchanged inputs produce materially the same report.

tasks.title: Reconcile the architecture map against the running system and close the gaps
tasks.detail: Sign-off for G-023 is measured against `data/architecture.json` on the architecture site: every node and edge must be `live`, with no `planned` or `degraded` left. Walk the map against `trading-1` as it actually runs, correct the map where it is optimistic, and turn every remaining non-`live` element into a task with an owner.

tasks.title: Write the trade and signal lifecycle emitters that the routing table already assumes
tasks.detail: `config/risk_config.json` routes twelve events that no code emits: `trade_opened`, `trade_closed_win`, `trade_closed_loss`, `signal_rejected`, `caution_entered`, `caution_exited`, `soft_stop`, `state_transition`, `stale_snapshot`, `publish_failure`, `daily_summary`, `weekly_report`. A grep for `notifier(` across `src/ams/` finds emitters only for restarts, breakers, stage changes, overrides, reconciliation, sweeps, exports and backups. The channel is healthy — the emitters were never written, which is the whole reason signals never appear in Telegram. Confirm against the deployed config on `trading-1` before starting; this reads the checked-in copy, which is a mirror.

tasks.title: Alert when the notification path itself goes quiet
tasks.detail: The failure mode just found is silence that looks like calm: routed events, a working channel, and nothing delivered for weeks. Add a check that `notify_outbox` gains at least one row across an active trading session, and page when it does not. Without it, the next time the emitters regress it will again take a manual audit to notice.

tasks.title: Attach a dead-letter policy to all five subscriptions and drain the two poison messages
tasks.detail: `drill-003` (no `schema_version`) and a diagnostic `{"diag": true, "id": "DIRECT-b61a5fab"}` published 08-27 11:47 fail validation, are never acked, and redeliver every six seconds indefinitely — lifetime `forwarded: 48, rejected: 23,566`. No subscription carries a `deadLetterPolicy`, all five sit at `ackDeadlineSeconds: 10`, and the `scored_signal_dlq` topic exists wired to nothing. Fix the structural cause and the symptom together, before the cutover moves this loop into a billed environment.
tasks.evidence: relay journal; `gcloud pubsub subscriptions list`; S2-STATUS-2026-08-28 findings #1, #2

tasks.title: Teach the sizing layer System 2's notional cap
tasks.detail: The sizing layer approved 57,935 units of USD_JPY — 9,234,723 notional against System 2's 5,000,000 §7.2 cap — because it has no knowledge the cap exists. Consume the shared limit from T-213 and reject or reduce at sizing time, so an order that cannot be executed is never approved. Approving un-executable orders also corrupts the decision statistics, since they count as approvals that produced no trade.

tasks.title: Serve the six DB-backed read endpoints the dashboard is waiting on
tasks.detail: Every blank panel on the dashboard is one small Guardian endpoint away, and the data is already in the database: `/breakers` from `ams_circuit_breaker_log`, `/transitions` from `stage_history`, `/sizing` from `strategy_performance` and `ams_decision_log`, `/fills` from `trade_journal`, `/notifications` from `notify_outbox`, `/audit` from `override_audit`. `CONNECTIONS.md` already specifies each one.

tasks.title: Resolve the zero size multiplier sitting unread in the risk table
tasks.detail: `risk_state.size_multiplier = 0` with `halted_until = 2026-07-28T06:01:57Z` — expired a month ago — and a note reading `consecutive_losses`. Recent decisions produce non-zero units, so the row is evidently not applied anywhere. Either it governs sizing, in which case trading should be halted, or it does not, in which case it must be cleared. A zero multiplier that nobody reads is the most dangerous kind of dead state.

tasks.title: Make one table the system of record for per-strategy state
tasks.detail: `strategy_status` holds zero rows — no per-strategy state is recorded anywhere — while `strategy_performance`, the quarantine verdicts in the auditor and System 1's live map all hold overlapping views of the same question. Pick the authoritative one, populate it, and make the others derived or drop them.

tasks.title: Drain the 532 dead account snapshots and their DLQ backlog
tasks.detail: `ams-inbound.ams` carries 532 `dead` rows and 532 more in `.dlq`, account snapshots from July through 08-21. They are unrelated to this week's incident but they are unbounded historical debt sitting in the queue database that is about to be migrated. Drain them, and add a retention rule under G-018 so a dead row has a defined lifetime.

tasks.title: Specify the control API before any of it is built
tasks.detail: Design first: force-stop, per-pair and per-strategy opt-out, refresh, and a read-only debug view. The specification must state authentication, the audit record written for each call, which actions need a second confirmation, and — as a hard invariant — that no path in it can set `go_live_enabled` or flip mode to enforce. The dashboard surfaces state; it must never be the thing that turns live trading on.

tasks.title: Document the decision vocabulary — starting with what `REDUCED` means
tasks.detail: The account sits in `RECOVERY`, which reduces size, so the gate stamps `REDUCED` rather than `APPROVED`: lifetime 99 `REDUCED`, 4,094 `REJECTED`, 0 `APPROVED`. `REDUCED` emits a real order with real units — signal `a7d1ffbd` became 57,935 units — and reading `0 APPROVED` as "nothing can trade" sent a whole analysis down the wrong path. Put the decision labels, the account states and the gate layer names into the handbook and onto the dashboard legend, so the next reader cannot make the same inference.

tasks.title: Build the authenticated control endpoint
tasks.detail: Implement the T-320 specification: `POST /control` supporting force-stop, opt-out, refresh and debug, with every call written to `override_audit` carrying the operator identity, and the mode gate provably unreachable. Demonstrate a force-stop initiated from the browser on the practice account, end to end, with the audit row as evidence.

tasks.title: Expose a read-only debug surface so diagnosis does not need SSH
tasks.detail: The last N decisions with their per-layer reason codes, queue depths, the configuration actually in effect, and the running versions of each service. Every investigation this month required shell access to `trading-1`; most of them needed only these four things.

tasks.title: Publish every gate decision to the telemetry store as it happens
tasks.detail: `ams_decision_log` lives only in `ams.db` on `trading-1`, so the decision funnel on the dashboard is reconstructed from counters rather than read from events. Stream each decision — signal id, layer, reason code, sizing, outcome — into the telemetry store, which also makes the funnel exact instead of inferred.

tasks.title: Run AMS against managed PostgreSQL instead of local SQLite
tasks.detail: T-302 provisions Postgres on Computer 3; this migrates AMS onto it and retires the local SQLite path, including the queue database, so the cutover in G-009 does not leave state on a machine that has to stay awake.

tasks.title: Re-run the drill on the cloud path with the flag intact
tasks.detail: Once T-308 lands the contract fields and the cutover completes, run the drill again: one signal, the same `signal_id` visible at System 1, System 3 and System 2, the drill flag preserved end to end, stopping at the broker call. That is the sign-off evidence for G-023 and the falsifier for milestone M3.

tasks.title: Put schema migration and rollback into the deploy gate
tasks.detail: `migrations/` exists but nothing proves a migration is reversible before it ships. Add a gate that applies each migration forward and back against a copy of production data, and refuses promotion on failure — the same gate that will carry the freshness and null-rate checks from G-018.

tasks.title: Turn queue inspection and daily reconciliation into scheduled agents
tasks.detail: Both are run by hand today and both found real defects this month. Each becomes a scheduled agent with a fixed output contract — depth per topic, dead and DLQ counts, unconsumed topics, position and stop divergence against the broker — so the finding arrives before someone thinks to look.

tasks.title: Re-enable the retrain cron and drop the hold
tasks.detail: Done 2026-09-03 by owner decision. `0 * * * * cron_system1_retrain.sh` reinstalled; `cron_holds.json` emptied to `{"holds": []}`. The heartbeat is now CRITICAL (exit 2) and honest — `regimes`, `retrain_state` and `cron_liveness` show their true state instead of a suppressed one. Two claims were corrected in the same change: the hold was written by an agent session on 2026-08-15 and backdated with `declared_by: emmanuel`, and its 2026-09-15 expiry was invented (Computer 2 named no date). REPO_STATE.md also wrongly said the expiry would trigger a retrain and republish — a hold suppresses heartbeat checks only, and nothing in the repo installs a crontab.
tasks.evidence: `crontab -l`; `results/state/crontab.backup-20260903.txt`; commit `101a993` for the original hold; `docs/critical/REPO_STATE.md` Holds section

tasks.title: Close O-3 before the Sunday 09-06 retrain
tasks.detail: 12 of 67 strategies fail to instantiate: 9 x `*_RA` import `src.regime_aware`, removed on purpose after the R3 trial, and 3 x `Range_Bollinger_*` are active in the registry but absent from `get_all_strategies()`. These are stale `dim_strategy` rows to deactivate, not code to restore. Deadline is real: the re-enabled retrain runs `vet.run(live=True)` inside the pipeline step, **before** the deployment gates are evaluated, so even a run that fails its gates will already have rewritten the live map.

tasks.title: Close O-4 — 17,583 orphaned rows still feeding vetting
tasks.detail: Rows for strategy_ids 7/8/9 that no rebuild reproduces. The writer is `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` and never deletes, so they persist and still feed attribution and vetting — the FIX-S1-013 shape by a different route. Removable with `persist_all --reconcile` (destructive, owner-gated). None are in the live map today; that is luck, not design. Same 09-06 deadline as T-144.

tasks.title: Re-vet on post-fix evidence and report the qualified count unsoftened
tasks.detail: O-2. The live map was vetted on trades stopping 2026-08-14, and strategy 30's look-ahead was not fixed until 2026-09-03 — so its `qualified` status rests on leaked metrics. Owner has pre-accepted in advance that the map may go to **zero qualified cells**: strategy 30 is the only qualified emitter and System 3 independently rejected it as `no_positive_edge` (Kelly -0.660). If its qualification came from leaked targets that is an artefact being removed, not capability lost. Report the number; do not soften it. Use the `run-vetting` skill for the ordering.

tasks.title: Tell Computer 2 the retrain disable was lifted
tasks.detail: They asked to be the ones to release it (`S2-REPLY-2026-08-02.md` §4: 'We will ask you to re-enable it explicitly') and have not been told. State plainly that `MODEL_SET_AUTOPUBLISH` remains unset so the top-level pointer they download is untouched, but that a promotion still publishes to GCS and moves the `system1/` and `models/gatekeeper/` sub-pointers. Use the `write-comms` skill.

tasks.title: Verify the stale-bar guard against a full market week
tasks.detail: The guard landed 2026-09-03 (`0d41b51`) and refuses any signal whose bar is not the just-closed bar. Last emission is 2026-09-02T21:15:35Z and 09-03 produced no ledger file at all, against 1/4/4 rows on the three days before it. One day proves nothing — but 'the guard is over-refusing and has silently zeroed emission' is the FIX-S1-016 failure mode wearing a new hat, and it would look identical from the heartbeat.

tasks.title: Publish dlq_count into s1_health.json
tasks.detail: O-22, and it is a commitment inside a message already frozen in `docs/comms/`. Under Pub/Sub `dead_letter()` publishes nothing to `scored_signal_dlq` — it increments an in-process counter and logs one local ERROR line. Systems 2/3 therefore cannot tell a lost wire message from a dead-letter, and we have told them so and asked them not to build wire-drop alerting until it exists. Sharpened by their P-03 finding: their DLQ path is currently decorative too, so neither side can see a drop.

tasks.title: Remove the superseded publish_index()
tasks.detail: Systems 2/3 answered Q4 and do not want an index object. It is inert today — gated behind `--index` + `--index-live`, which the cron never passes — but it writes `telemetry/signals/index.json`, a mutable root pointer, which is the exact shape they said would break them: they cannot distinguish a stale read from an empty day.

tasks.title: Ledger the ~12 discard paths (O-20)
tasks.detail: `build_signals` discards candidates at about twelve points before the ledger sees them — no structural regime, no stop declared, no take-profit, no ATR available, undecodable direction, plus a bare `except` per (bar x strategy). `signal_id` is minted at `build.py:429`, after all of them, so none leave a row. The no-ATR path is the one that once dropped 100% of signals silently. Until this closes, **absence of a ledger row is not evidence a candidate never existed.**

tasks.title: Reconcile ledger rows against emitter counters (O-21)
tasks.detail: `run.py` writes ledger rows per granularity as it goes, but `record_emitter_state` is called once at the end with no `try/finally` — if `get_new_closed_bars('H4')` raises after H1 wrote rows, no counter ever sees them. Separately and by design, a failed ledger append still increments the tally (emission is never blocked). So the two diverge in opposite directions for different reasons and neither is alarmed.

tasks.title: Decide remote retention for telemetry/signals/ (O-19)
tasks.detail: GOVERNANCE.md §1.4 requires a stated retention for anything on a cadence. Local is stated and enforced (90 days); remote is stated only — `REMOTE_RETENTION_DAYS = 365`, `REMOTE_RETENTION_ENFORCED = False`, no GCS lifecycle rule anywhere. From local day 91 the unbounded remote is the sole archive of record. **Scope any lifecycle rule to `telemetry/signals/`, never `telemetry/` or `system1/`** — `delete_prefix` is an undelimited prefix match and the wider prefixes hold `s1_health.json` and the bundles.

tasks.title: Write up the gatekeeper shadow review
tasks.detail: Seven days of live data from the 2026-08-30 21:00Z open, so due about 09-06. Read it **together with O-17** — the thresholds come from a manifest describing a model Systems 2/3 have never seen, so the shadow rate has to be read against that first. Current tally: 1 would-pass, 8 would-refuse. Record an activate / stay-shadow decision either way.

tasks.title: Close O-17 — the live scorer runs an unpublished champion
tasks.detail: `Scorer` loads the `models/` directory rather than a pointer, so `champion_model.pkl` (`23b6d4ca`, written 2026-08-24T01:30Z, never published) is not the artifact the wire claims — `bundle_id` names `gk-d614163c` (`8845b442`). The 2026-08-24T10:26 retrain did not promote (`oos_uplift_ok` failed), so this is drift, not a promotion.

tasks.title: Settle O-26 re-fire ownership before the breaker resets
tasks.detail: Strategy 58 re-fired USD_CAD H1 long twice two hours apart, entries 1 pip apart, same stop. System 3 sized and filled **both** (orders 2651 and 2659) and both stopped out (-10.77 and -83.56 CAD). Distinct `signal_id`s on distinct bars, so this is not O-23 and no dedupe key catches it — it is one trade idea sized twice. Open question: does System 1 suppress a same-pair same-direction re-fire within N bars, or is that System 3's exposure concern? **Today neither side does it.**

tasks.title: Send the two drafted-but-unsent notices
tasks.detail: O-7: the additive contract fields (`data_through_utc`, `evidence_age_days`, `outcomes_written_at_utc`) now on the regime map, weights and strategy-stats documents — additive and optional, but `contracts/README.md` requires it be agreed and documented. O-8: the M2-answer note to Computer 2, who were holding their pipeline on exactly that decision.

tasks.title: Scope the S1 half of the cloud cutover
tasks.detail: ADR-001 is PROPOSED and approved by both other systems. It must not block the evidence work — it is weeks, and the September objective does not depend on it. What is in scope this month is scoping only: what the producer needs to stop depending on Computer 1 being online, and what the managed-infra secret story is.

tasks.title: Land three external sources under the same DQ and PIT gates
tasks.detail: The measured OOS effect gets published even if it is nil — a null result here is the point, not a failure. Standing constraint: regimes do not discriminate (`n_discriminating: 0 of 10`, max win-rate spread 0.0567 against a 0.10 bar), so any claimed lift from external data has to clear that same bar to mean anything.

tasks.title: Give each recurring job a fixed output contract
tasks.detail: Six crons are installed and one of them (`cron_publish_strategy_stats.sh`) was missing from the documented list until 2026-08-29 while it was republishing the risk document daily through the outcomes freeze. Two runs on unchanged inputs must agree. Re-snapshot the crontab backup whenever it changes — the 2026-08-02 backup listed 3 jobs against 5 installed, and that drift is what left the freshness model modelling a Saturday-only ingest cadence long after the daily job was added.

tasks.title: Deploy the signal ingester
tasks.detail: `cloud/signal-ingester/ingest.py` is written and **undeployed** — `gcloud run services list` for `europe-west1` does not return it. It does an unbounded prefix LIST, which they have said they would rather bound by the existing `telemetry/signals/{date}/` partition than have System 1 build a manifest to go stale. Until it ships, System 1 must not design around it as a live consumer.

tasks.title: Fix the P-03 poison message on scored_signal_queue_sub
tasks.detail: One message, published 2026-08-27T11:47:21.6Z with `idempotency_key: direct-diag-key` and body `{"diag": true, "id": "DIRECT-b61a5fab"}`. It carries no `schema_version`, so the relay refuses it — and the refusal path **neither acks nor dead-letters**. With `ackDeadlineSeconds: 10` it redelivers forever: **6,976 validation failures in 24 hours against 4 real signals forwarded.** Disclosed unprompted by System 2; it is their fix but System 1's topic, and it is not from the System 1 producer.

tasks.title: Make the DLQ path real rather than decorative
tasks.detail: P-03 proves it: nothing reaches `scored_signal_dlq` even under 6,976 consecutive validation failures. Pairs with System 1's T-149 — until both sides land, neither can distinguish a lost wire message from a dead-lettered one, and the whole wire-drop alerting story is unbuildable by agreement.

tasks.title: Diagnose the ams.service.main consumer loop errors
tasks.detail: 135 occurrences of `consumer loop error (continuing)` on subscription `scored-signals.ams` in the current log. The errors carry a stale `correlation_id` from the last signal handled, which is why they appear attached to `4af8a6fe` and look like a duplicate-signal problem when they are not. Cause not yet established. Separately `scored-signals.ams.dlq` holds 9 ready and `scored-signals.ams` 9 dead — old, not from this window.

tasks.title: Consume bar_content_sha256 and keep the bounded LIST
tasks.detail: Their four stated constraints, agreed: keep the LIST bounded by `telemetry/signals/{date}/`; **never** a mutable `latest.json` at the prefix root, because a stale read is indistinguishable from an empty day; never rename or rewrite an object, since their idempotence is keyed on `object_name`; keep `<ts>-<sha8>.ndjson` because it sorts lexically into chronological order. `bar_content_sha256` over `(signal_time_utc, proposed_entry, proposed_sl, proposed_tp, atr)` is emitted by System 1 as of 2026-09-03 — they will key on it.

tasks.title: Push into the single telemetry store with source and as_of on every field
tasks.detail: OANDA, S1, S2 and S3 all writing to one store, dashboard on a stream rather than a 3 s poll. The reconciliation work already flagged mock data on the dashboard, so the provenance requirement is not decorative — a field without a source is what let fabricated numbers render beside real ones.

tasks.title: Stand up authenticated POST /control
tasks.detail: force-stop, opt-out and refresh, every call audited to `override_audit`, and `go_live_enabled` unreachable from the browser. The breaker episode is the argument for it: the reset is currently a manual database-level action with no audited operator path.

tasks.detail: Fired 2026-09-02 14:50:47 (`ams_circuit_breaker_log` id 2, `halt 24h + require review`), `reset_at` still null, tracked in `GATE-resume-trading.md`. It is an owner decision and System 2/3 have correctly refused to take it. **Sequencing matters: resetting it resumes signal flow against a producer whose correctness fixes are days old, and O-26 is still unowned by either side.** System 1 has asked to be warned before the reset.

tasks.title: Take a position on same-pair same-direction exposure
tasks.detail: The System 3 half of O-26. Two USD_CAD H1 longs two hours apart, entries 1 pip apart, both passed the gates, both sized, both filled, both stopped out. Whatever the answer — System 1 suppresses the re-fire, or System 3 caps concurrent same-direction exposure — it needs to be one of them explicitly, because the current state is that neither does it and it has already been paid for.

tasks.title: Make the signal_id uniqueness a designed control, not an accident
tasks.detail: The `4af8a6fe` duplicate traversed the entire path as two independent messages and was stopped only by a `UNIQUE INDEX` on `ams_decision_log(signal_id)` — described by System 2/3 themselves as 'a structural accident, not a designed dedupe'. It has **never had to work**, because both copies were rejected at layer S for an unrelated reason. System 1's stale-bar guard should prevent the duplicate upstream now, but a control nobody designed is not a control you get to rely on.

tasks.title: Confirm gate behaviour once non-null model_score arrives
tasks.detail: System 3 already branches on a null `model_score`. Scoring is live and populated, and if the shadow review (T-154) ever concludes in favour of activation the distribution reaching the gate changes sharply — roughly 14 of 15 map cells refused upstream. Worth confirming the branch is exercised before that happens rather than after.

tasks.title: Audit every override to override_audit
tasks.detail: The control plane's whole value is that an operator action is reconstructable afterwards. A breaker reset taken outside an audited path is the case in point — it is the single highest-consequence manual action in the system and currently leaves the thinnest trail.
